subject.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): keep blank credentials from overriding AWS auth

question: Is process-wide deletion of blank AWS credential environment variables an acceptable authentication boundary for the bundled Bedrock and Mantle providers?
rationale: The patch appears technically focused, but approving global `process.env` mutation requires direct lifecycle and concurrency inspection that the failed review sandbox could not perform.

options.title: Approve provider sanitization
options.body: Accept deletion of whitespace-only AWS credential variables before Bedrock credential resolution after confirming no unrelated concurrent path depends on their presence.

options.title: Use isolated credential providers
options.body: Require constructing an AWS credential environment or provider chain that ignores blank values without mutating process-wide environment state.

options.title: Pause pending deeper review
options.body: Keep the PR open until a Bedrock area owner can inspect lifecycle, concurrency, and duplicated Mantle behavior directly.

recommendation.title: Approve provider sanitization
recommendation.body: Accept deletion of whitespace-only AWS credential variables before Bedrock credential resolution after confirming no unrelated concurrent path depends on their presence.

likelyOwner.reason: No Bedrock-specific history owner could be established because repository history commands could not run; this is the best available low-confidence escalation route.
